utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please be seated. Mr Registrar, please have the accused brought in and have them sit in the order that was arranged for them to sit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please be seated. I would like the accused to be helped with their headsets. Please be seated. Do you hear me? Does everybody hear? Does the Defence hear, the accused, do they hear? If you hear, please be seated. Registrar, would you please give us the references for this case?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is case IT-95-16-I, the Prosecutor of the Tribunal against Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vlatko Kupreskic, Vladimir Santic, also known as "Vlado", Stipo Alilovic, also known as "Brko", Drago Josipovic, Marinko Katava, Dragan Papic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: First I would like to identify the different parties. Prosecutor, what are the appearances for the Prosecution, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr President and your Honours, good morning counsel. My name is Mark Harmon, I will be representing the Prosecutor's Office this morning. Assisting me will be Mr Gregory Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, would you please give us your name, what bar you are a member of and tell us, since you are the only one here, tell us whether you are representing all six of the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr President, your Honours, good day, my name is Petar Pavkovic, I am an attorney from Zagreb, I am a member of the Croatian Bar Association. In your brief, you have the documents confirming my statement. I am Defence counsel for the accused Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vladimir Santic, also known as "Vlado", Drago Josipovic, Marinko Katava and Dragan Papic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You may be seated. I will now turn to the accused in the order that the security officers and the Registrar placed them and I would ask that when each one of the names is called that each person would rise, tell us his name, family and given names, and his current residence, as well as place and date of birth. I will start with Dragan Papic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Do you hear me?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I hear. My name is Dragan Papic, I was born on 15th July 1967, in the village of Santici, a locality near Vitez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Your attorney is Mr Pavkovic, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, you may be seated. I would like to call Mr Marinko Katava.

utterances.speaker: MR. KATAVA
utterances.text: My name --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Tell us your name, both first and last, the date and place of birth, and your current domicile.

utterances.speaker: MR. KATAVA
utterances.text: My name is Marinko Katava, I was born on 18th November 1952 in Busovaca. I am living in Vitez. The attorney representing me is Mr Petar Pavkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. I now call the gentleman next to you, Mr Drago Josipovic. Would you confirm that for us, please? Tell us your name, date and place of birth and where you now have domicile.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSIPOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Drago Josipovic, I was born on 14th February 1955 in Santici near Vitez, and I am a permanent resident of Santici where I am living now. The attorney representing me is Petar Pavkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, you may be seated. Mr Santic, Vladimir?

utterances.speaker: MR. SANTIC
utterances.text: My name is Vladimir Santic, I was born on 1st April 1958, in Donja Veceriska, in the municipality of Vitez. My residence is in Vitez, Kinkresmir, 4th Street. The attorney representing me is Mr Petar Pavkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, you may be seated. The man next to you, who should be Mr Mirjan Kupreskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIRJAN KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: My name is Mirjan Kupreskic, I was born on 21st October 1963 in Vitez, I am now living in Pirici, a village near Vitez, and Mr Petar Pavkovic is my attorney.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, you may be seated. Now I call Mr Zoran Kupreskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORAN KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: My name is Zoran Kupreskic, I was born on 23rd September 1958 in Vitez, I am now living in Vitez and the gentleman representing me is Petar Pavkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You may be seated. You are appearing for the first time before the International Criminal Tribunal, with the Prosecution being represented by Mr Kehoe and Mr Harmon, who drafted an indictment which will be read to you in a few moments, for you to understand what is going on. I must remind you of the text from the Statute which the Security Council drafted and which constituted our Tribunal, that is Articles 20 and 21 and Rule 62, which provide for what is to be done and give you certain advantages which are the rights of the accused and will explain what is going to happen at this hearing. Article 20 of the Statute states that a Trial Chamber shall have the indictment read, satisfy that the rights of the accused are respected, confirm that the accused understands the indictment and instruct the accused to enter a plea. In this same Statute, in Article 21, there are a series of rights that are given for you, including the right to be informed promptly, in a language which you understand, in detail, of the nature and the cause of the charge or charges brought against you. As regards this hearing, this is covered by Rule 62 of the Rules, which state that the Trial Chamber first will satisfy that the right of the accused to counsel is respected, which is the case, by the fact that we have Mr Pavkovic here; then reads or has the indictment read to the accused, in a language they speak and understand, which we will do in a few moments; and then calls upon the accused to state whether they understand the indictment, after which the accused are called upon to enter a plea of guilty or not guilty on each count in the indictment which has just been read for them. Should the accused fail to do so, the Trial Chamber will enter a plea of not guilty on his behalf. In case of a plea of not guilty, he will instruct the Registrar to set a date for trial. In case there is a plea of guilty, instruct the Registrar to set a date for the pre-sentencing hearing. All of these formalities, which are very important, both for you and for the work of the Tribunal, govern what we will do. I now turn to your Defence attorney and ask whether he was in a position to give each of his clients a copy of the indictment in their own language and I ask whether they have understood the contents, even though we are going to re-read it. Mr Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr President, my clients have received the indictment, they have read it, and understood the charges against them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you, please be seated. I will now ask the Registrar to read the entire indictment. Registrar, would you please read the indictment which was drafted by the Prosecutor at a date which you will state to us. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr President, it is the indictment dated 2nd November 1995. The Prosecutor against Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vlatko Kupreskic, Vladimir Santic, also known as "Vlado", Stipo Alilovic, also known as "Brko", Drago Josipovic, Marinko Katava, Dragan Papic. Indictment. Richard J Goldstone, Prosecutor of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia, pursuant to his authority under Article 18 of the Statute of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia (Tribunal Statute) alleges that: 1. On 6 March 1992, the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina (BiH) declared its independence. 2. From at least 3 July 1992, the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna (HZ-BH) considered itself an independent political entity inside the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. 3. From at least January 1993 until at least the end of May 1993, the HZ-HB armed forces, known as the Croatian Defence Council (HVO) were engaged in an international armed conflict with the armed forces of the government of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. 4. From the outset of hostilities in January 1993, the HVO systematically attacked villages chiefly inhabited by Bosnian Muslims in the Lasva River Valley Region in Central Bosnia-Herzegovina. These attacks resulted in the death and wounding of numerous civilians. 5. The persecution of Bosnian Muslim civilians escalated in frequency throughout the early part of 1993, culminating in simultaneous attacks throughout the Lasva Valley region on 16 April 1993. 6. On 16 April 1993, at approximately 5.30 am, HVO forces attacked the town of Vitez and the nearby villages of Donje Veceriska, Sivrino Selo, Santici, Ahmici, Nadioci, Stari Bila, Gacice, Pirici and Preocica. All the villages are within a 10 kilometre radius from the village of Ahmici. 7. The pattern of attack was the same across the area. The villages were first shelled with an assortment of weaponry including mortars, rockets and anti-aircraft guns. Groups of HVO soldiers then went from house to house killing and wounding Muslim civilians and finally burning houses, barns and livestock. After the attacks subsided, large numbers of civilians were detained. The offensive which lasted several days was a highly co-ordinated military operation involving hundreds of HVO troops. 8. After the villages were attacked, Bosnian Muslim civilians were arrested and taken to various detention centres. While imprisoned, the HVO brought Bosnian Muslim male detainees to the frontlines to dig trenches, subjecting those detainees to the cross fire between the HVO and the BiH armies. 9. One of the villages where Bosnian Muslim detainees were forced to dig trenches in the midst of sniper fire was at Pirici, a small hamlet adjacent to Ahmici, Vitez. The accused. 10. Zoran Kupreskic, son of Anto and brother of Mirjan, was born on 23 September 1958 in the village of Pirici. He was an HVO soldier in the Ahmici area. Before the war, he operated a business in Ahmici with his cousin Vlatko Kupreskic. 11. Mirjan Kupreskic, son of Anto, was born on 21 October 1963 in the town of Vitez. With his brother Zoran and cousin Vlatko Kupreskic, he was a HVO soldier in Ahmici. 12. Vlatko Kupreskic, son of Franjo, was born on 1 January 1958 in the village of Pirici. He lived and worked in Ahmici where he owned a business with his cousin Zoran Kupreskic before the war. He and his cousins, Zoran and Mirjan Kupreskic, were HVO soldiers. 13. Vladimir Santic also known as "Vlado" was born on 1 April 1958 in Donja Veceriska. Prior to the war he lived in Vitez and was a policeman by profession. He was an HVO soldier in Vitez. 14. Stipo Alilovic also known as "Brko" was born in Nadioci. He lived in Vitez and was an HVO soldier in Vitez. 15. Drago Josipovic, son of Niko, was born on 14 February 1955 in Santici. Before the war, he was a chemical worker by profession. He was an HVO soldier in Santici. 16. Marinko Katava, a member of the HVO in Vitez. He also lived in Vitez and his wife was a pharmacist. 17. Dragan Papic was born in the village of Santici on 15 July 1967. He lived in Ahmici, Vitez and was an HVO soldier. General allegations. 18. At all times relevant to this indictment, the acts and omissions alleged in this indictment took place during April 1993 in the Lasva River Valley Region in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the territory of the former Yugoslavia. 19. At all times relevant to this indictment, a state of international armed conflict and partial occupation existed in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the territory of the former Yugoslavia. 20. All acts or omissions set forth herein as grave breaches of the Geneva Conventions of 1949 (grave breaches) and recognised by Article 2 of the Tribunal Statute occurred during that armed conflict and partial occupation. 21. At all times relevant to this indictment, the victims referred to in the charges contained herein were persons protected by the Geneva Conventions of 1949. 22. At all times relevant to this indictment, the accused were required to abide by the laws and customs governing the conduct of war. 23. Each of the accused is individually responsible for the crimes alleged against him in this indictment, pursuant to Article 7(1) of the Tribunal Statute. Individual criminal responsibility includes committing, planning, instigating, ordering or otherwise aiding and abetting in the planning, preparation or execution of any crimes referred to in Articles 2 to 5 of the Tribunal Statute. 24. The general allegations contained in paragraphs 1 through 9 and 18 through 23 are realleged and incorporated into each of the charges set forth below. Charges. 25. When HVO forces attacked villages and towns in the Lasva Valley Region on 16 April 1993, the village of Ahmici experienced the most significant killing and destruction. Located approximately 5 kilometres east of Vitez, Ahmici had a population of approximately 466 inhabitants, with 356 being of Muslim ethnicity and 87 of Croat ethnicity prior to April 16 1993. After the attack, there were no Bosnia Muslims still living in Ahmici. 26. Using a similar pattern of attack used for other villages, the HVO attack on Ahmici targeted houses, stables, sheds and livestock owned by Muslim civilians. The HVO first shelled Ahmici from a distance, then groups of soldiers went from house to house, attacking civilians and their properties using flammable tracer rounds and explosives. Several houses were destroyed by pouring inflammable liquid on the outside or inside and setting it on fire. Every Muslim owned house in Ahmici was burned, and many unarmed Muslim civilians were deliberately and systematically shot. At least 41 civilians were killed and numerous others were wounded. 27. In the neighbourhood of Zume, in Ahmici, witnesses observed approximately 100 HVO soldiers on their way to the village, and ten minutes later on their way back from the village. In the interim, numerous houses in Zume were set on fire and a large proportion of the Muslim inhabitants were killed. 28. Between 150 and 200 Muslim civilians sought refuge in the house of a Muslim civilian in Gornji Ahmici. When UNPROFOR forces of the British Battalion came to the village at about 12.00 hours the HVO stopped shooting, but the shooting immediately resumed when British battalion left. The HVO forces then fired directly at the house where the civilians were hiding, both with an anti-aircraft gun and other artillery. At about 20.00 hours, the 150 to 200 civilians were able to evacuate the house and fled to the mosque in Vrhovine, two kilometres north of Ahmici. 29. Numerous Bosnian Muslim civilians were arrested and were taken to detention centres. The detainees were told they were being held for exchange, but also as hostages if the HVO was defeated by the BiH armies on the frontlines. Many detainees were taken to the frontlines near Ahmici, to the village of Pirici, to dig protective trenches. 30. A minimum of 103 Muslim civilians were killed in and around Ahmici. Of the 103 persons killed, 33 were women and children. All 176 Muslim houses in Ahmici, along with the mosque, were destroyed. Counts 1-2. 31. Between 16 April 1993 on or about until 25 April 1993, all of the accused were HVO soldiers who participated in an unlawful attack against the civilian population and individual citizens of the village of Ahmici causing death and injury to that civilian population and individual citizens and the total destruction of the Muslim homes in the village. By the foregoing acts and omissions the accused individually and in concert with others committed the following crimes: Count 1: Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vlatko Kupreskic, Vladimir Santic, Stipo Alilovic, Drago Josipovic, Marinko Katava and Dragan Papic participated in the unlawful and wanton destruction of property not justified by military necessity, a grave breach recognised by Article 2(d) of the Tribunal Statute; and Count 2: Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vlatko Kupreskic, Vlado Santic, Stipo Alilovic, Drago Josipovic, Marinko Katava and Dragan Papic participated in the deliberate attack on the civilian population and the wanton destruction of a village, a violation of the laws and customs of war recognised by Article 3 of the Tribunal Statute. Counts 3-8. 32. When the attack on Ahmici commenced in the early morning hours of 16 April 1993, Sakib Ahmic was residing with his son, Naser Ahmic, Naser's wife, Zehrudina, and his two children Elvis (four years of age) and Sejad (three months of age). 33. Armed with an automatic weapon, Zoran Kupreskic, entered the house and shot and killed Naser Ahmic. Zoran Kupreskic then shot and wounded Zehrudina. 34. When Mirjan Kupreskic entered the Ahmic house, he poured flammable liquid onto the furniture to set the house on fire. Gunfire was then directed toward the two children, Elvis and Sejad Ahmic. When Sakib Ahmic fled the burning residence, Zehrudina, who was wounded, was still alive, but ultimately perished in the fire. 35. Naser Ahmic, Zehrudina Ahmic, Elvis Ahmic and Sejad Ahmic all died and Sakib Ahmic received burns over his head, face and hands. By the foregoing acts and omissions, the accused individually and in concert with others committed the following crimes: Count 3: Zoran Kupreskic participated in the wilful killing of Naser Ahmic, a grave breach, recognised by Articles 2(a) of the Tribunal Statute; Count 4: Zoran Kupreskic participated in the murder of Naser Ahmic, a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Article 3 of the Tribunal Statute; Count 5: Zoran Kupreskic and Mirjan Kupreskic participated in the wilful killing of Zehrudina Ahmic, Elvis Ahmic and Sejad Ahmic, a grave breach recognised by Article 2(a) of the Tribunal Statute; Count 6: Zoran Kupreskic and Mirjan Kupreskic participated in the murder of Zehrudina Ahmic, Elvis Ahmic and Sejad Ahmic, a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Article 3 of the Tribunal Statute; Count 7: Zoran Kupreskic and Mirjan Kupreskic participated in wilfully causing Sakib Ahmic great suffering or serious injury to body or health, a grave breach recognised by Article 2(c) of the Tribunal Statute; and Count 8: Zoran Kupreskic and Mirjan Kupreskic participated in wilfully subjecting Sakib Ahmic to cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Article 3 of the Tribunal's Statute. Counts 9-12. 36: Prior to the 16 April attack, HVO soldiers armed with automatic rifles congregated at the residence of Vlatko Kupreskic in Ahmici. When the attack commenced, HVO units departed from Vlatko Kupreskic's residence. Other HVO soldiers shot at Bosnian Muslim civilians from Vlatko's house throughout the attack. 37. As the shooting continued, members of the Pezer family, who were Bosnian Muslims, gathered in their shelter to hide from HVO soldiers. Shortly thereafter, the Pezer family, along with other Bosnian Muslims who had also taken refuge in the shelter, decided to escape through the forest. 38. As the Pezer family ran toward the forest with the other Bosnian Muslims, past Vlatko Kupreskic's house, Vlatko Kupreskic and other HVO soldiers in the house began to shoot at the group. Fata Pezer, the wife of Ismail Pezer, was shot and killed while their daughter Dzenana Pezer and another Bosnian Muslim civilian were shot and wounded. As a result of the foregoing acts and omissions, the accused committed individually and in concert with others committed the following crimes: Count 9: Vlatko Kupreskic participated in the wilful killing of Fata Pezer, a grave breach recognised by Article 2(a) of the Tribunal Statute; Count 10: Vlatko Kupreskic participated in the murder of Fata Pezer, a violation of the laws and customs of war recognised by Article 3 of the Tribunal Statute; Count 11: Vlatko Kupreskic participated in wilfully causing Dzenana Pezer and a Bosnian Muslim civilian great suffering or serious injury to body or health, a grave breach recognised by Article 2(c) of the Tribunal Statute; Count 12: Vlatko Kupreskic subjected Dzenana Pezer and a Bosnian Muslim civilian to cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war, recognised by Article 3 of the Tribunal Statute. Counts 13-14. 39. In another part of Ahmici, the home of Musafer and Suhreta Puscul was attacked by numerous HVO soldiers while the family slept. 40. Several HVO soldiers who participated in the attacks were neighbours of the Puscul family such as Zeljko Livancic (deceased). Other HVO soldiers who participated in the attack and were known to the Puscul family include the following accused: Vladimir Santic, Stipo Alilovic, Drago Josipovic and Marinko Katava. 41. After an unidentified HVO soldier ordered Musafer Puscul and his family from their home, Zeljo Livancic (deceased), Vladimir Santic, Drago Josipovic and Marinko Katava, took Musafer Puscul behind a nearby shed, and shot and killed him while Stipo Alilovic held Mustafa's family at gunpoint. 42. Thereafter all of the HVO soldiers including Vladimir Santic, the group's commander, went into the Puscul's home, vandalised it, and set it ablaze. Upon leaving the premises, HVO soldiers shot flammable bullets into the residence, starting additional fires at various locations in the home. By the foregoing acts and omissions, the accused individually and in concert with others committed the following crimes: Count 13: Vladimir Santic, Drago Josipovic, Marinko Katava and Stipo Alilovic participated in the wilful killing of Musafer Puscul, a grave breach recognised by Article 2(a) of the Tribunal Statute; Count 14: Vladimir Santic, Drago Josipovic, Marinko Katava and Stipo Alilovic participated in the murder of Musafer Puscul, a violation of the laws and custom of war recognised by Article 3 of the Tribunal Statute. Counts 15-16. 43. After the Ahmici attack on 16 April, Bosnian Muslims were taken into custody and were used as forced labour. Specifically, they were compelled to dig protective trenches at Pirici, a village adjacent to Ahmici, by Dragan Papic and other HVO soldiers. While digging trenches, the detainees were fed only one meal per day and were frequently exposed to the cross fire between the HVO and BiH armies. At least one Bosnian Muslim male was shot by an unknown sniper while digging trenches at Pirici. By the following acts and omissions, the accused individually and in concert with others committed the following crimes: Count 15: Dragan Papic participated in the unlawful confinement of civilians, a grave breach recognised by Article 2(g) of the Tribunal's Statute; and Count 16: Dragan Papic participated in outrages upon the personal dignity of another, a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Article 3 of the Tribunal's Statute. Counts 17-18. 44. The accused Dragan Papic and other HVO soldiers continued to force Bosnian Muslim prisoners to dig trenches from approximately 16 April 1993 until approximately 25 April 1993. 45. During this period of time, one of the Bosnian Muslim detainees named Jusuf Ibrakovic, also known as "Jusa", attempted to escape. He was recaptured and beaten by Dragan Papic and other HVO soldiers. The accused Dragan Papic and another HVO soldier then shot and killed Jusuf Ibrakovic while he lay unconscious on the ground. By the foregoing acts and omissions, the accused individually and in concert with others committed the following crimes: Count 17: Dragan Papic participated in the unlawful killing of Jusuf Ibrakovic, a grave breach recognised by Article 2(a) of the Tribunal's Statute; and Count 18: Dragan Papic participated in the murder of Jusuf Ibrakovic, a violation of the laws or customs or war recognised by Article 3 of the Tribunal's Statute. 2 November 1995, The Hague, The Netherlands, signed Richard J Goldstone, Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr Registrar. First I would like to turn to the Defence and ask the attorney the following so that it is understood. The entire indictment was just read and you have seen that two names relate to people who are not here among the accused, that is Vlatko Kupreskic and Stipo Alilovic. In a moment, on behalf of the Tribunal, I will make sure that the accused understood the indictment, and then we will ask them whether they plead guilty or not guilty. I wanted to be very clear that the accused present for those parts of the indictment that concern them will answer for those parts. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is clear, Mr President. They have read this and they have understood everything. You have indicated correctly the two persons listed in the indictment are not present here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr Pavkovic. I would now like to turn to the Prosecutor, to say that in the French version, everything that involves Count 2 is translated as "violations graves". I would like this -- that is "infractions graves" in french, not "violations graves". "Violations des lois ou coutumes de guerre", but "infractions graves" for Article 2. I think this affects the French text only in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, I agree, Mr President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I will now ask each accused to rise when his name is called and ask whether he understood the contents of the indictment in the language that he understands and then ask him to state to the Tribunal whether he pleads guilty or not guilty. I insist upon this notion which is part of our Rules of procedure and evidence which I call to you and which I reread to you. You must state for each of the counts against you whether you have chosen to plead guilty or not guilty. I will ask you to rise, I will first ask Mr Zoran Kupreskic to rise. Mr Zoran Kupreskic, did you hear the indictment and did you understand it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORAN KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: I heard the indictment and I understood it well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Specifically those parts that concern you. I will recall the counts one by one and ask you to state whether you plead guilty or not guilty. Count 1, unlawful and wanton destruction of property not justified by military necessity, which is a grave breach of Article 2(d) of the Tribunal Statute. Do you plead or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORAN KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: I am fully innocent as regards this count.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, but we use the notion of pleading guilty or not guilty. I do not know whether the interpreters are interpreting it properly. In the Rules it states that you must say -- if you feel guilty, you can state that at the proper time through your attorney, but for the time being, we are asking you to make a choice of one or the other, please. You can plead guilty, say I am guilty, I can claim that there were mitigating circumstances, or I can plead not guilty. I ask the interpreters to be careful who translates the interpretation of this nuance.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORAN KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Fine. Count 2, deliberate attack on the civilian population and wanton destruction of a village, which are violations of the laws and customs of war recognised by Article 3 of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORAN KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 3, the killing of Naser Ahmic, which is a grave breach of the Geneva Convention, 2(a) of the Tribunal Statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORAN KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 4, murder of Naser Ahmic, which would be a violation of the laws and customs of war for the Prosecutor recognised by Article 3 of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORAN KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 5, wilful killing of Zehrudina Ahmic, Elvis Ahmic and Sejad Ahmic, a grave breach recognised by Article 2(a) of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORAN KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 6, the murder of Zehrudina Ahmic, Elvis Ahmic and Sejad Ahmic, which would be a violation of the laws or customs of war, pursuant to Article 3 of the Tribunal Statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORAN KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 7, wilfully causing great suffering or serious injury to body or health or Sakib Ahmic, which would be a grave breach, recognised by Article 2(c) of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORAN KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 8, wilfully subjecting cruel treatment on Sakib Ahmic which would be a violation of the laws or customs of war, recognised by Article 3 of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORAN KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr Zoran Kupreskic, you may be seated. I now call Mr Mirjan Kupreskic, and ask the same questions. Did you hear those parts of the indictment specifically that concern you and did you understand it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIRJAN KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We will now do the same as we did before. For Count 1, wanton destruction of property not justified by military means, Article 2(d) of the Statute. Do you plead guilty?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIRJAN KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: I feel not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 2, deliberate attack on the civilian population and wanton destruction of a village which would be a violation of the laws or customs of war, recognised by Article 3 of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIRJAN KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: I feel not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He says he feels not guilty. Is that his plea? That is the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: This may be an interpretation problem. I will now say to Mr Pavkovic, to make sure one can understand the procedure, one can feel innocent, but one must plead guilty or not guilty. You see the nuance there, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: The pleading of this accused person corresponds to his attitude towards the counts, the charges, therefore it may be accepted if he pleads in this manner. In essence it is one and the same thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Karibi-Whyte. This is a point which had to be clarified. We can now continue. Count 5. Wilful killing of Zehrudina Ahmic, Elvis Ahmic and Sejad Ahmic, a grave breach recognised by Article 2(a) of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIRJAN KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 6, murder of Zehrudina Ahmic, Elvis Ahmic and Sejad Ahmic, which would be a violation of the laws or customs of war, recognised by Article 3 of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIRJAN KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 7, wilfully causing great suffering or serious injury to body or health on Sakib Ahmic, which would be a grave breach recognised by Article 2(c) of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIRJAN KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 8, wilfully subjecting cruel treatment on Sakib Ahmic, according to Article 3, would be a violation of the laws or customs of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIRJAN KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please be seated, Mr Mirjan Kupreskic. I will now ask Mr Vladimir Santic to rise. Did you hear the indictment, did you understand its contents, Mr Vladimir Santic?

utterances.speaker: MR. SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have understood the indictment referring to me in full.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I will proceed the same way as I have just done for the two before you. For Count 1, unlawful and wanton destruction of property not justified by military necessity, a grave breach of the general is a convention and Article 2(d) of the Tribunal Statute. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: MR. SANTIC
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 2, deliberate attack on the civilian population and wanton destruction of a village, which would be a violation of the laws or customs of war, pursuant to Article 3 of the Tribunal Statute. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: MR. SANTIC
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 13, wilful killing of Musafer Puscul, a grave breach covered by Article 2(a) of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. SANTIC
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 14, the murder of Musafer Puscul, which would be a violation of the laws or customs of war, recognised by Article 3 of the Statute; do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: MR. SANTIC
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You may be seated. I will now ask Mr Drago Josipovic to rise. First of all, did you hear the indictment in its entirety and did you understand those parts concerning yourself?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSIPOVIC
utterances.text: I have understood it fully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I will call out each count and ask you to state whether you plead guilty or not guilty. For Count 1, unlawful and wanton destruction of property not justified by military necessity, recognised by Article 2(d) of our Statute, and would therefore be a grave breach of the Geneva Convention. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSIPOVIC
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 2, deliberate attack on the civilian population and wanton destruction of a village pursuant to Article 3 would be a violation of the laws and customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSIPOVIC
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 13, the wilful killing of Musafer Puscul, a grave breach recognised by Article 2(a) of the Statute; do you plead guilty or not guilty.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSIPOVIC
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 14, the murder of Musafer Puscul, which would be a violation of the laws or customs of war, recognised by Article 3 of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSIPOVIC
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You may be seated. Mr Marinko Katava, would you rise, please? Did you hear the indictment and did you understand it, especially those parts which refer to yourself?

utterances.speaker: MR. KATAVA
utterances.text: I heard it and I understood it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: For Count 1, unlawful and wanton destruction of property not justified by military necessity, which would be a grave breach of the Geneva Convention recognised by Article 2(d) of the Tribunal Statute; do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: MR. KATAVA
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: For Count 2, the deliberate attack on the civilian population and wanton destruction of a village, which would be a violation of the laws or customs of war, pursuant to Article 3 of the International Criminal Tribunal's Statute, do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: MR. KATAVA
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 13, wilful killing of Musafer Puscul, which would be a grave breach recognised by Article 2(a) of the Statute; do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: MR. KATAVA
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: For Count 14, the murder of Musafer Puscul, a violation of the wars and customs of war, recognised by Article 3 of our Statute; do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: MR. KATAVA
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please be seated. Mr Dragan Papic, did you hear the indictment and did you understand it, those parts concerning yourself?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAPIC
utterances.text: I have heard the indictment and I understood it fully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: For Count 1 in this indictment, unlawful and wanton destruction of property not justified by military necessity, which would be a grave breach of the Geneva Conventions recognised by Article 2(d) of the Tribunal's Statute, do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAPIC
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: For Count 2, the deliberate attack on the civilian population and wanton destruction of a village, which would be a violation of the laws and customs of war, recognised by Article 3 of the Tribunal's Statute, do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAPIC
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: For Count 15, unlawful confinement of civilians, a grave breach recognised by 2(g) of our Statute, do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAPIC
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: For Count 16, participation in outrages upon the personal dignity of another, the violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Article 3 of the Tribunal Statute, do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAPIC
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: For Count 17, unlawful killing of Jusuf Ibrakovic, which would be a grave breach recognised by Article 2(a) of the Tribunal Statute, do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAPIC
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: And for Count 18, the murder of Jusuf Ibrakovic, a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Article 3 of the Tribunal Statute, do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAPIC
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You may be seated. I now again turn to Mr Pavkovic and say that we consider that this declaration by which the accused state that they feel not guilty is the same thing as being statements of -- pleas of not guilty for procedural matters, which allows you therefore to plead not guilty before this Tribunal. Do we agree to that, Mr Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr President, I have understood you and I agree with your interpretation of this issue. So if you will allow me, if I may say a few words in conclusion, all the accused present here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Excuse me, the hearing is not completed yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please be seated. I will ask the Registrar to note all of the pleas of not guilty. Before giving you back the floor Mr Pavkovic, I would like to speak about the organisation of the Trial Chamber's work. I would like to turn to the Prosecutor and recall his obligations which are covered by Rule 66 of the Tribunal, which say that he shall make available to the Defence as soon as practicable all copies of the supporting material which accompanied the indictment when confirmation was sought, as well as all prior statements obtained by the Prosecutor from the accused or from Prosecution witnesses. Where are we as far as this goes? What have you done as far as this is concerned, Mr Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr President, we are gathering those materials and we will provide them to the Defence within two weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. The Tribunal notes that in two weeks Mr Pavkovic should receive all of the supporting material for the indictment when confirmation was being sought, as well as prior statements of the accused and the statements of any witnesses which were taken. I also point out to you and recall that according to the text in force at this Tribunal that, starting from today, that is the day of the initial appearance of the accused, that is October 8th 1997, we have 60 days in order to file any preliminary motions which are provided for under Rules 72 and 73 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. We should set the date for a status conference in order to review the status of the work, but perhaps this is premature to set the date for the status conference. What is your opinion about this, Mr Pavkovic? After that I will ask for the Prosecutor's opinion. Mr Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I must say first of all that I as the Defence counsel accept this deadline of two weeks for the submission of the supporting material attached to the indictment. As for the status conference, we would be grateful if that would be held as soon as possible and we the Defence counsel will make every effort to contribute to that. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr Pavkovic. I would like to point -- Mr Harmon? You heard what Mr Pavkovic said.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr President, I believe that the setting of a date for the status conference is premature at this point in time. I note that counsel represents six accused and until the issues of multiple representation are clarified, I do not think we can have a meaningful status conference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr Pavkovic, the Prosecutor has just raised an issue, a question which we would have asked. You are the single Defence for the six accused. Would it be indiscreet to ask you whether you will be alone in the future or whether you have thought about the possible conflicts of interest, whether there are other people who will work with you, or are you only alone for today? You can answer that as you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have already said that we as the Defence counsel will do everything in our power and I do not think that the Prosecutor should be concerned with the position of the Defence counsel. I am here today representing all the accused, but as the trial progresses, I will only be defending the accused Marinko Katava, and you have in the court record the powers of attorney of other Defence counsel for the other accused. So just a minor correction, except for I will also be defending Drago Josipovic, and you have my power of attorney in the court record. I have submitted it to the Registry. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you for these clarifications, which were noted by the Registrar. I would like, however, to raise two issues. The first is a material question, but which has an effect on our work. We have only one courtroom, and therefore would be even premature to set a trial date. In addition to that, you realise that the judges of this Tribunal, at least some of them, are reaching the end of their mandate which will expire on 17th November. Others were elected by the General Assembly of the United Nations. It may be that after 17th November there will be a change in the composition of this Trial Chamber. There may be a change in the Defence composition and therefore in the Trial Chamber as well, but all of this will be made clear. I would like to ask whether Mr Pavkovic has any other comments he would like to make. You may speak before we adjourn the hearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have no other comments to make. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr President, I have no additional comments. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I turn to my colleagues; have you any comments, Judge Karibi-Whyte?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: No, I have not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Judge Shahabuddeen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: No comments at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Shahabuddeen. I would like to conclude. In order to implement the texts in their entirety -- it is difficult to set a trial date, but I would like to hear your opinion about this, Mr Registrar, so that the transcript will express officially what is happening.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It would be difficult for us to suggest a trial date at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Since there are no other comments, this hearing stands adjourned.
